title: RFID Inventory
summary:
The meeting covered upcoming demos, RFID inventory architecture, and improved implementation and consulting models. The transfer-order demo for Simkhai was targeted for Wednesday, including virtual, consignment, and customer locations; the Dollskill demo and script were targeted for Tuesday. Dollskill’s preorder-provider contract expires in mid-September, with a month-to-month extension available. Malbon feedback and a potential near-term start were also discussed.

The RFID solution should maintain each item’s serialized EPC in the backend while deriving UPC information for inventory operations. The architecture requires an intermediate hardware-software layer for Bluetooth RFID readers, deduplication, decoding, encoding, printing, and integration with existing inventory systems. Vendor partnership may accelerate hardware, printer, encoding, and API capabilities.

The team identified handheld readers for receiving and cycle counts, fixed readers for checkout and store-location monitoring, and RFID printers for retagging. Existing receiving, fulfillment, transfer, and cycle-counting workflows could be adapted to serialized RFID scans, while receiving must validate and place goods into stock. Serialized tracking was preferred over aggregate UPC conversion, but stray reads, lost or missing tags, damaged goods, tailoring, returns, and physically segregated inventory require defined controls.

POS selling remains the most difficult component. RFID tags must be associated with Shopify order items and passed to the OMS without disrupting checkout. Shopify lacks a standard RFID integration, so the proposed approach uses an iPad application that listens to the reader and sends data through a Shopify POS extension; end-to-end validation remained incomplete.

The meeting also identified weaknesses in implementation project management, including reactive configuration and the absence of a standard go-live checklist. A lightweight checklist may be more effective than creating Jira tasks for every item. The participants discussed potential paid coordination and consulting support, including deeper order-routing guidance and a stronger roll-off process that enables clients to operate independently after hypercare.
